newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/13.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/13.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 12.0/13.0 percent on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said the central bank's injection of 1.002 trillion rupiah in the morning seemed to be sufficient to meet overall demand at the month-end.
One local bank dealer said longer-term rates were declining as fears of a tight market diminished. One-week money was last at 12.0/12.5 percent and one-month at 12.50/12.75 percent.
They said ample rupiah supply drove short-term swaps lower, with overnight swaps easing to 0.35/0.42 from 0.45/0.55 points.
The central bank offered one-to-two day bilateral papers (SBIs) at 5.5 percent, one-week at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 17.25 percent, compared with 14.77 percent on Monday.
Bond dealers said prices remained firm after rising on Tuesday by some 25 to 50 basis points.
